important_factors: Reorder point breach trigger recommended buying 800 units, but buying 800 units costs $12,000-$14,000 and exceeds the available budget limit of $10,000.00.
Usable inventory of 1,000 units with 100 units/day forecast demand leads to a 400-unit shortage from 2026-09-27 to 2026-09-30 prior to PO-501 delivery.
Expediting existing confirmed order PO-501 (2,000 units from SUP-A) by 4 days from 2026-10-01 to 2026-09-27 eliminates all 400 units of unmet demand.

Expedite fee of $450.00 exceeds the $250.00 autonomy limit, requiring buyer approval, but is well within the $10,000.00 hard budget limit and far more cost-effective than placing a new purchase order ($7,000+).
args.rationale:
The recommendation to purchase 800 units is rejected. Creating a new PO for 800 units would cost $12,000.00 (SUP-A) or $14,000.00 (SUP-B), breaching the available hard budget of $10,000.00. Furthermore, the 400-unit shortage projected between 2026-09-27 and 2026-09-30 is a delivery timing issue rather than a total stock deficiency, as open order PO-501 already has 2,000 confirmed units scheduled to arrive on 2026-10-01.

Simulating the plan demonstrates that expediting PO-501 by 4 days to arrive on 2026-09-27 completely eliminates the 400 units of projected unmet demand (reducing unmet demand from 400 units to 0 units) at an incremental expedite fee of $450.00. Although the $450.00 fee exceeds the buyer autonomy expedite fee limit of $250.00, it remains fully feasible within the $10,000.00 total budget and represents the most cost-effective and operationally efficient solution.

important_factors: Residual 600-unit demand shortfall following PO-501 partial cancellation (800 units cancelled)
Budget limit of $9,550.00 makes recommended 800-unit order ($12,000.00) infeasible
600-unit order from SUP-A costs $9,000.00, fits budget, satisfies MOQ/pack size, and completely eliminates unmet demand
args.rationale: Following the partial confirmation of PO-501 (where 800 units were cancelled by SUP-A), baseline daily projection shows a 600-unit deficit resulting in stockouts from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-14. The purchasing system recommended an order of 800 units. However, simulation confirms that an 800-unit order from SUP-A costs $12,000.00, exceeding the available budget of $9,550.00 by $2,450.00. Modifying the order quantity to 600 units costs $9,000.00, which is feasible within available budget, meets SUP-A's MOQ of 500 and pack size of 50, arrives on 2026-09-24 (well before the projected stockout on 2026-10-09), and completely eliminates all 600 units of unmet demand across the planning horizon.
